title: Shared create-branch action with three entry points (+8 more)
request:
# Shared create-branch action with three entry points (and 8 more)

This request comes from a conversation with the developer about their app.
Anything marked suspected or not checked is a guess: confirm it in the code before building on it.

## What this is about
The Git features can switch branches, but they cannot create, rename or delete local branches, and they cannot do anything with tags except show them in History. The developer wants local branch operations (including a new branch from detached HEAD and from a History commit), full tagging (local tags plus pushing a tag and deleting a tag on the remote), and right-click menus in the History graph ('git tree') with a keyboard path for every action. In the same feature, the Git drawer and the Add/Edit app pane move onto the shared Zest-based SidePane. SidePane gets a new non-blocking mode for these two panes so the app keeps one consistent look and the app behind the panes stays usable.

## What to build or fix

### 1. Shared create-branch action with three entry points (confirmed)
Add one backend command that creates a local branch from a given start point (a branch name or commit hash), with an option to switch to it afterwards. Check the name with the existing valid_branch_name, take the per-repo OpGuard lock the way switch_branch does, and show git's error text when it fails (for example, the name already exists). There are three entry points, all using this one action. (1) 'New branch' from the current branch, in the branch pane (BranchMenu), with a 'switch to it' option. (2) 'New branch here' when HEAD is detached. The GitBar shows 'detached @ <hash>' there and Pull/Push/Sync are disabled. This creates the branch at the current HEAD and switches to it, so the user gets back onto a branch without losing their place. Offer it on the current commit's right-click menu in History and in the branch pane. (3) 'New branch from this commit' on a History commit row, starting from that commit, with the same 'switch to it' option. After a create or switch, refresh the branch list, the status and History.

Evidence:
- src-tauri/src/git.rs:316-323 valid_branch_name
- src-tauri/src/git.rs:325-338 switch_branch runs `git switch <name>` under OpGuard::acquire (line 330)
- src-tauri/src/git.rs:281-313 branches() lists refs/heads and refs/remotes via for-each-ref, with the current branch
- src-tauri/src/git.rs:192-193 detached flag
- src/features/git/GitBar.tsx:58 shows 'detached @ <hash>'
- src/features/git/GitBar.tsx:103-111 Pull/Push/Sync disabled={off || !onBranch}
- src/features/git/HistoryView.tsx:45 rows only toggle expand/collapse
- src/features/git/BranchMenu.tsx:8, 26, 39-49 title 'Switch branch', only an onPick action per branch
- Developer: 'Both: new branch from detached HEAD and from a History commit'

### 2. Rename a local branch (confirmed)
Add a backend command to rename a local branch (git branch -m <old> <new>). Check the new name with valid_branch_name and run it under the OpGuard lock. If git refuses (for example, the target name exists), show git's message. Reach it from the branch pane and from the right-click menu on a branch label in History. Refresh the branch list and History afterwards. Local only: this does not rename or touch any remote branch or upstream.

Evidence:
- src-tauri/src/git.rs:316-323 valid_branch_name
- src-tauri/src/git.rs:330 OpGuard::acquire
- src/features/git/BranchMenu.tsx:39-49 only switching is offered today
- Developer accepted create/rename/delete scope

### 3. Delete a local branch: safe first, force only after confirmation (confirmed)
Add a backend command to delete a local branch. The current branch can never be deleted: refuse it in the backend and hide or disable it in the UI. First run a safe delete (git branch -d <name>). If git refuses because the branch is not fully merged, do not delete anything yet. Warn the user that the branch has unmerged commits and ask them to confirm. Only after they confirm, run git branch -D <name>. Run it under the OpGuard lock and show git's message for any other failure. Reach it from the branch pane and the right-click menu on a branch label in History. Local only: deleting on the remote is not part of this.

Evidence:
- src-tauri/src/git.rs:330 OpGuard::acquire
- src-tauri/src/git.rs:281-313 branches() already knows the current branch
- Developer: 'Warn it's unmerged, then force delete if you confirm'

### 4. Local tags: create (lightweight or annotated), list, delete (confirmed)
The app has no tag support beyond showing 'tag: <name>' in History decorations. branches() reads only refs/heads and refs/remotes. Add backend commands to list tags, create a tag on any commit (lightweight, or annotated with a message: git tag <name> <commit> or git tag -a <name> -m <msg> <commit>), and delete a local tag (git tag -d <name>). Validate the tag name: reuse valid_branch_name or an equivalent ref-name check (git check-ref-format style). Run the commands under the OpGuard lock. Reach 'New tag on this commit' from the History commit-row right-click menu, and 'Delete tag' from the right-click menu on a tag label. Refresh History afterwards so the labels update.

Evidence:
- src-tauri/src/git.rs:527 refs parsed from log decorations only
- src-tauri/src/git.rs:812 test expects 'tag: v1' in refs
- src-tauri/src/git.rs:284 for-each-ref refs/heads refs/remotes only
- Developer: 'Also add full tagging support'

### 5. Remote tags: push one tag, delete a tag on the remote (confirmed)
Add 'Push tag' (git push <remote> refs/tags/<name>) and 'Delete tag on remote' (git push <remote> --delete refs/tags/<name>), both on the right-click menu of a tag label. Reuse the existing push plumbing: remote_name() and its clear 'no remote' error, OpGuard, NET_TIMEOUT and net_error(). Never force: if the remote already has a same-name tag on a different commit, git refuses, and the app shows git's message. Deleting a tag on the remote must ask for confirmation first, because others may already have fetched it. Plain `git push` does not send tags today, and this does not change that.

Evidence:
- src-tauri/src/git.rs:450 '/// Never forces.'
- src-tauri/src/git.rs:457-460 remote_name, no-remote message, OpGuard::acquire
- src-tauri/src/git.rs:462 run(top, &["push"] ...) with NET_TIMEOUT; line 469 net_error
- Developer: 'Local, plus push and delete-on-remote for tags'

### 6. Right-click menus in the History graph and branch pane, with keyboard access (confirmed)
There is no context menu anywhere in the app today, so build a small reusable one. In the History graph ('git tree', HistoryView.tsx): a commit row gets 'New branch from this commit' and 'New tag on this commit', and the current commit also gets 'New branch here' when HEAD is detached. A branch label gets Switch, Rename and Delete. A tag label gets Push tag, Delete tag and Delete tag on remote. Branch entries in the branch pane get the same branch actions. Today each History row is one button that only toggles open/closed, and ref names are plain <span className={styles.ref}> labels. They need to become targetable (focusable) so a label can have its own menu without breaking row expand/collapse. Keyboard: the menu key and Shift+F10 on a focused row or label open the same menu, and the branch pane offers the same actions, so nothing is mouse-only. Escape closes the menu.

Evidence:
- Grep 'onContextMenu|contextmenu|ContextMenu' in src/: no matches
- src/features/git/HistoryView.tsx:45 onClick={() => toggle(r.commit.hash)}
- src/features/git/HistoryView.tsx:62-66 refs rendered as <span className={styles.ref}>
- Developer: 'you didn't confirm if the git features shall be available in gittree via right click context menu' (confirmed yes)

### 7. Non-blocking mode for SidePane (confirmed)
SidePane always wraps ZestResponsiveLayout in its own full-window overlay (position: fixed; inset: 0; z-index: 50), which dims and blocks the app on purpose. Add an opt-in non-blocking mode (for example a prop) that skips this overlay div, turns off the package's desktop overlay (enableDesktopOverlay false) and sets sidePane.nonModal. The pane keeps the Zest look and theme colours. Close and Escape work as before. The app behind it stays clickable and usable. Default behaviour must not change: Dialog and BranchMenu stay blocking. Check at runtime how the package's nonModal behaves: that clicks reach the app behind the pane on desktop, and how it looks on narrow/mobile widths.

Evidence:
- src/features/apps/SidePane.tsx:2 import { ZestResponsiveLayout } from 'jattac.libs.web.zest-responsive-layout'
- src/features/apps/SidePane.tsx:31-37 comment: keeps the desktop overlay purely dimming
- src/features/apps/SidePane.tsx:52-72 overlay div always wraps ZestResponsiveLayout
- src/features/apps/SidePane.module.css:1-7 .overlay position: fixed; inset: 0; z-index: 50 ('it blocks the app behind it')
- node_modules/jattac.libs.web.zest-responsive-layout/dist/UI/ZestResponsiveLayout.d.ts:16 nonModal?: boolean
- node_modules/jattac.libs.web.zest-responsive-layout/dist/UI/ZestResponsiveLayout.d.ts:24-25 enableDesktopOverlay, closeOnDesktopOverlayClick
- Developer: 'Add a non-blocking SidePane mode for these two panes'

### 8. Move the Git drawer onto SidePane (non-blocking) (confirmed)
GitDrawer is a hand-made <aside> styled as an absolute right-edge panel (min(560px, 100%)). Move it onto SidePane in the new non-blocking mode, so it looks like the other Zest panes while the rest of the app stays usable as it is today. Keep its current contents, open/close behaviour and Escape handling. Remove the now-unused .drawer styles.

Evidence:
- src/features/git/GitDrawer.tsx:24 <aside className={styles.drawer}>
- src/features/git/Git.module.css:131-137 .drawer position: absolute; right: 0; width: min(560px, 100%)
- src/features/git/BranchMenu.tsx:3, 26 and src/features/apps/Dialog.tsx:2, 27 already use SidePane
- Developer: 'for all those other sidepanes e.g the one used by git and app addition, migrate them to use zest responsive layout'; 'Fold it into the branch/tag feature'

### 9. Move the Add/Edit app pane onto SidePane (non-blocking) (confirmed)
EditPane is a hand-made <aside> styled as an absolute right-edge panel (min(460px, 100%)). Move it onto SidePane in the new non-blocking mode, keeping its fields, save/cancel, Close and Escape behaviour, and keeping the app behind it usable. Remove the now-unused .pane styles.

Evidence:
- src/features/apps/EditPane.tsx:236 <aside className={styles.pane}>
- src/features/apps/EditPane.module.css:1-7 .pane position: absolute; right: 0; width: min(460px, 100%)
- Developer: 'Add a non-blocking SidePane mode for these two panes'

## Not part of this
- Remote branch operations: pushing a branch, deleting a branch on the remote, setting an upstream
- Stash-and-switch when uncommitted changes block a switch. Today git refuses and nothing is lost (src-tauri/src/git.rs:704-716), and that stays as is
- Merge. Pull stays fast-forward only (src-tauri/src/git.rs:424, 443)
- Conflict resolution, including Hakiri-suggested resolutions with rationale and human override (conflicts are detected at src-tauri/src/git.rs:232 and block the commit at src/state/git.ts:64-65). This is a separate later feature and waits for the Hakiri JSON stdin/stdout wrapper
- Hakiri-generated default commit message (src/features/git/ChangesView.tsx:13, 58). This is a separate later feature and waits for the Hakiri JSON stdin/stdout wrapper
- Any bridge to Hakiri, a .NET 10 library. Lite-commander has no .NET code or sidecar, and the bridge design is deferred until Hakiri's developer ships the wrapper
- Changing Dialog or BranchMenu: they stay blocking

## Not settled yet (do not treat as fact)
- How the Zest package's sidePane.nonModal behaves at runtime (desktop click-through to the app behind it, narrow/mobile layout) has not been seen. Check it during the build, and if it cannot give a usable non-blocking pane, raise it with the developer rather than falling back to the blocking overlay

## Requirements agreed in the conversation

The developer and the assistant already agreed these while talking. Build on them; do not ask again what they settle.

- **R1**: A developer can switch the repository to any local branch from the branch menu, and choosing a remote branch with no matching local branch creates that local branch and switches to it.
  - Done when: Choosing a local branch in the branch menu makes that branch the checked-out branch
  - Done when: Choosing a remote branch with no matching local branch creates the local branch and checks it out
- **R2**: A developer can create a new local branch from a starting point - the current branch, the current commit in detached HEAD, or a past commit chosen in the History view - and choose whether to switch to it; rename a local branch; and delete a local branch other than the one currently checked out. Deleting a branch whose commits are not merged anywhere first warns the developer that the work is unmerged and deletes it only after the developer confirms.
  - Done when: Creating a branch from the current branch with a valid unused name adds it to the branch menu and it can be checked out
  - Done when: When creating a branch the developer can choose whether to switch to it right away
  - Done when: In detached HEAD, creating a branch here starts it at the current HEAD commit and can switch to it, putting the developer back on a branch at that commit
  - Done when: From a History row, creating a branch from this commit starts it at that commit, with the option to switch to it
  - Done when: Renaming a local branch changes its name in the branch menu without changing its commits
  - Done when: Deleting a local branch removes it from the branch menu
  - Done when: Deleting a branch whose work is not merged warns that its commits are unmerged and deletes it only after the developer confirms
  - Done when: Deleting a branch whose work is already merged deletes it without an unmerged-work warning
- **R3**: A developer can merge a chosen branch into the currently checked-out branch from inside the app.
  - Done when: Merging a branch that is ahead fast-forwards the current branch without creating a merge commit
  - Done when: Merging diverged branches creates a merge commit when there are no conflicts, or stops in a clear conflict state when there are
  - Done when: A merge that is already in progress is shown when the app or git view opens
- **R4**: For each conflict produced by a merge, the app asks Hakiri for a proposed resolution and shows a brief rationale, and the developer can accept it, edit it, or reject it before anything is committed.
  - Done when: Each conflicted file shows Hakiri's proposed resolution and a short rationale
  - Done when: The developer can accept the proposal, edit the resolved content, or reject it and resolve manually
  - Done when: No conflict resolution is committed until the developer explicitly commits
- **R5**: On the commit screen, the developer can ask Hakiri to fill the commit message box with a default message based on the files and changes observed in the working tree; the generated message stays editable.
  - Done when: Requesting a default message fills the commit message box with text derived from the observed changes
  - Done when: The developer can edit the generated message before committing
  - Done when: Committing uses the text currently in the box
- **R6**: A developer can create a tag on any commit - either a lightweight tag or an annotated tag carrying a message - see the tags listed on their commits in the History view, delete a tag locally, push a single tag to the remote, and delete a tag on the remote.
  - Done when: Creating a lightweight tag on a commit makes it appear on that commit in the History view and in the tag list
  - Done when: Creating an annotated tag with a message stores that message and shows the tag on the commit
  - Done when: Deleting a tag locally removes it from the History view and the tag list without changing any commits
  - Done when: Pushing a tag sends that single tag to the remote without changing any commits
  - Done when: Deleting a tag on the remote removes it from the remote after the developer confirms, and leaves the local tag in place
- **R7**: The branch, commit and tag actions are reachable by right-clicking the relevant row or label in the git tree, and the same actions are reachable without a mouse from the keyboard and from visible controls.
  - Done when: Right-clicking a commit row offers New branch from this commit and New tag on this commit
  - Done when: Right-clicking a branch label or a branch in the branch pane offers Switch, Rename and Delete
  - Done when: Right-clicking a tag label offers Push tag, Delete tag locally and Delete tag on remote
  - Done when: The same actions are reachable from the keyboard (menu key or Shift+F10 on the focused row) and from visible controls in the branch pane
  - Done when: In detached HEAD, the current commit's menu offers New branch here
- **R8**: As part of the branch and tag feature, the side panes that are still hand-built - the Git panel and the Add/Edit app pane - move onto the app's shared Zest responsive layout in a non-blocking mode, so they keep the shared look and theme colours while the rest of the app stays usable behind them. Dialogs and the branch picker stay blocking as they are now. They are delivered together with the branch and tag work, not as a separate feature.
  - Done when: The Git panel uses the shared Zest side-pane layout instead of its hand-made panel
  - Done when: The Add/Edit app pane uses the shared Zest side-pane layout instead of its hand-made panel
  - Done when: The Git panel and the Add/Edit app pane open in a non-blocking mode, so the rest of the app stays visible, does not dim, and can still be clicked and used while the pane is open
  - Done when: The branch picker and dialogs stay blocking as they are today
  - Done when: The migrated panes keep the shared pane's theme colours, open and close the same way, and still respond to Escape
  - Done when: All existing actions in the Git panel and the Add/Edit app pane still work after the move

Not part of this: Changing pull from fast-forward-only to creating merge commits; Automatically committing merge results or Hakiri-proposed resolutions; Creating, renaming or deleting branches on the remote, and setting branch upstreams; Fetching tags from the remote or automatically syncing tags between local and remote; Conflict resolution outside the merge flow, such as pull or rebase conflicts; Push, fetch or history rewriting beyond the branch, merge, tag and commit operations above; Building the Hakiri JSON-over-stdin/stdout/stderr wrapper, which Hakiri's developer is providing; Switching branches with uncommitted changes by stashing and carrying the work across, which was raised and deferred as its own feature; Redesigning app surfaces beyond moving the Git panel and the Add/Edit app pane onto the shared Zest layout; Making dialogs or the branch picker non-blocking, which stays as it is today
